limitations: Use booking-final.patch/source/manifest for the combined nine-file booking change, or apply phase3 after phase2. The old phase2 frozen migration used a salon-wide early lock and must not be released alone.

Only schema/function/permission metadata was read from the linked Supabase project. No live booking RPC, data creation, schema or permission change, payments, notification delivery, commit, push or deployment.

The isolated tests use actual booking, scheduling and ranking SQL against minimal tables. Identity/capability and time-policy helpers are synthetic fixtures, deposits are null-configured except POS rejection checks, and notification delivery is stubbed. Auth/PostgREST/RLS/session behavior has not been verified end to end.

Portable POS now explicitly acquires the same existing ranking advisory lock before rechecking a missing contact. Migration fails closed if that ranking lock signature or expected function anchors changed; future ranking lock changes must update this dependency.

Current retry-key behavior is preserved: scope is salon plus exact key, without adding actor/payload scoping or a unique index. Hash collisions can only serialize unrelated keys; SQL lookup retains the full key.

Docker context is correct; dockerInference is an internal Desktop socket, not a context. Starting or choosing the existing contexts cannot repair the inaccessible runtime reparse point. Windows/Docker runtime repair is outside the allowed start/context-only intervention. No evidence supports promising that a reset, delete, permission change or reinstall is necessary or safe; none was attempted.
Full release baseline assembly/build and authenticated isolated E2E remain required for launch confidence. No assertion that all possible multi-function lock cycles are eliminated.
Salon creation root cause remains unconfirmed: the local sanitized lookup log still has startup only. Manual authenticated lookup reproduction is still needed.
